title: Does extension preservation eliminate stratified intensional negation?
area: Database theory and finite model theory
formal: For every finite input schema and every generic query q expressible by a safe, constant-free stratified Datalog program with disequality, suppose that q is preserved under induced extensions of finite database instances. Must q be expressible by a safe, constant-free semi-positive Datalog program with disequality over the same input schema and with the same output arity? In the source’s notation, is Str-\(Datalog(\ne ) \cap  E = Sp-Datalog(\ne )\)? Preservation under induced extensions is defined below. The inclusion from right to left is known; the question is the converse.
context:
Ordinary monotonicity permits adding arbitrary facts, including facts involving only existing values. Induced-extension preservation permits new values and facts involving them while keeping every old tuple’s membership fixed. Confusing these two conditions changes the source question.

The desired program may test absence of an input fact. What it must eliminate is negation of derived relations across strata. This is therefore different from asking for a completely positive Datalog definition.

Ketsman and Koch separate several monotone and positive Datalog fragments, but explicitly leave this extension-preservation equality open. The known semi-positive inclusion does not supply the reverse inclusion.

Dawar and Sankaran’s 2021 paper builds extension-preserved properties with strong first-order quantifier-prefix requirements. Its notation \(Datalog(\neg )\) permits only extensional negation and disequality. Those results do not establish a separation between the stratified and semi-positive classes asked about here.
why: Would characterize when a semantic guarantee about growing databases suffices to remove negation between recursive stages, clarifying the expressive resources needed for distributed queries.
status_note: Recovered the exact equality from the 2020 conclusion and checked the finite-instance, safety, disequality and stratification conventions. Checked subsequent extension-preservation literature and searched for this equality and domain-distinct monotonicity; no matching resolution was located as of 12 September 2026. This search is not exhaustive and is not an independent mathematical proof of openness.

sentences: Stratified Datalog can negate relations already computed in earlier stages.
Semi-positive Datalog only negates input relations.
The question asks whether preserving answers when new values extend a database always permits the simpler semi-positive form.
The input growth must preserve every relation on tuples of old values, which differs from unrestricted monotonicity.
The source leaves this converse expressiveness question open, and the checked later first-order preservation results do not resolve it.

answer_criterion: Prove that every query satisfying the stated stratified definability and extension-preservation conditions has a semi-positive definition, or exhibit a stratified extension-preserved query and prove that no semi-positive program with disequality defines it. Failure of one proposed rewrite is insufficient. The claim concerns existence of equivalent definitions; it imposes neither an effective recognition algorithm for E nor a bound on rewrite size.
